course_name_original: Ciencia e Ingeniería de los Materiales (0241819)

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire theoretical and practical knowledge related to the study and evaluation of the composition, microstructure, and properties of materials.
Learn and identify the Microstructure of Materials. Properties, applications, and in-service behavior of metallic, polymeric, ceramic, and composite materials.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of materials science, technology and chemistry. Understand the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing and material properties.
Know the thermal and thermomechanical treatments of materials and their effect.
Know the criteria for material selection, their in-service behavior and causes of failure.
Able to perform laboratory tests to characterize material behavior.
Able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.

teaching_methods: Classroom presentation of concepts and problem-solving sessions, including discussion classes and common sharing.
Laboratory activities of increasing difficulty to develop autonomy in problem-solving.
Personal study, report writing, practical exercises, etc. as independent work.
assessment_rules: Students can pass by continuous assessment, which requires completing the practicals. The theoretical part accounts for 85% (divided into three partial exams, each 33% of the theoretical part), and the laboratories account for 15%. To pass by continuous assessment, the weighted average must be greater than 5, with each partial exam grade being above 4. A minimum grade of 4 is required in all evaluated parts. If a student fails continuous assessment, or in the ordinary call exam, they must take a final exam covering all course content (lectures, seminars, practicals); if practicals were approved, their grade is retained and this part does not need to be re-examined. In the extraordinary call exam, no part of the subject grade is retained.
